main_text.p: (quo nullum est arctiùs, nullum sacratiùs) vinculo obstrinxit : [ Omnis anima &c. ] ⁴Id est, ac si diceret {*}Salmeron. Ief. sanctus Paulus (ait Salmeron Ief.) non turbentur Principes, Reges, aut Imperatores, neque seuiant in Christiani nomine Professores, quia nihil innouauit præceptor meus Christus, quo ladat eorum potestatem, cælestia prædicans, terrens contemnens ; nec eripit mortalia, qui regna dat cælestia. Hæc Ille.

Antequam aliò pergamus, Bellarminus rursus compellandus est, sæpè à nobis monitus, multùmque monendus vt suis præsidiis diffidat, nec ea testimonia obijciat, in quibus plerunque non solùm ab Authoribus, quos citat, sed etiam à seipso citante refutatur. Cuius ofcitantiæ specimen iam præbet, dicit enim {+}Paulum EiuSupra.verbis [Omnis anima potestatibus præeminetibus subditi sit] generaliter loqui hortarique vt omnes subditi suis Superioribus pareant tàm spiritualibus quàm temporalibus : ex qua sententia (inquit) non potest deduci Papam subiectum esse Regi, nec Regem Papæ. Hæc Bellarminus. Disputo. Hæc Apostoli Propositio de subiectione erga sublimiores potestates vel generaliter accipienda est, de quauis potestate sublimiori ; vel spiritualiter de subiectione erga potestatem secularem. Si generaliter, & tamen (vt ais) Regem Papæ subiectum esse non probat ; tùm erras planissimè, dum afferis ex hoc {*}Docerì eminentiam potestatis Pontificiæ super potestatem Regum & Principum terrenorumBellar. supra : nam verba Apostoli disertissima sunt, [Omnis anima sublimioribus potestatibus subdita sit.] Sin verò Paulus specialiter intelligit Potestates seculares, tùm Papa subijcitur Impp. quia dicitur, [Omnis anima sublimioribus potestatibus subdita sit :] nisi forsan exanimem faciatis Papam. Annon vtroque cornu confoderis? Hactenùs de loco Pauli; ad Bernardum reuertor.Bernarde & post

page.notes: Cap. 5 running head read as printed. Marks: "⁴" and "*" are printed beside the Salmeron and Bellarminus notes; the exact pairing of the asterisk marks with their notes is not fully clear at this scan resolution. The reference "Paulum Eiu" ends in a word I read as "Eiu" (probably Eius); the last letter is uncertain. The note "sest. 11." beside the line "[Omnis anima" (lower half) could not be confirmed and is omitted. Left margin: no text. Right margin notes are small and partly blurred: "quæsupra." (beside "cipes") and "Bellar supra" may read differently. Watermark "Digitized by Google" at the lower right is excluded. Catchword "Expli-" and signature "Cc 2" read from the foot of the page.
